Political economy

Political economy studies how political institutions and economic incentives shape policy and economic outcomes. It is useful for understanding why policies differ across settings and why economically desirable reforms may face political constraints.

The subject also connects distributional consequences with political behaviour. Studying who gains and who loses from a policy can help explain political support, opposition, institutional persistence, and the implementation of reforms.
